_bio: Security Specialist Keisha Williams, Floor 2 Ward B. Ex-Marine, facility security — fought back during the 'evacuation drill' that was actually a harvest sweep; they took her FOR the combat genes. Warrior companion. Full romance arc (equals, sparring cadence). Sidequest: find Officer James Torres, her partner from second shift.

nodes.line: *she's still breathing hard, staring at the man she was just under, jaw tight* He was warm, and then you— *she looks at you, hard* Don't make me say the soft part. Just tell me the THING is out of me. Then you're real, and my knife's in my left boot — they missed it. Cut me out.

choices.text: (take the knife, cut the straps) It knew. I made sure.
(cut her loose) You're safe now.
First tell me you're still you.

nodes.line: *she's worked one strap half loose with her teeth. Her wrists are raw.* Either shoot me or cut me loose, but decide fast — I've been at this strap forty minutes and I am NOT being here when they come back to finish the job.

choices.text: (cut her loose) Easy, soldier. I've got you.
Forty minutes? You almost had it.

nodes.line: Good. GOOD. *she's off the table before the last strap clears, shaking the blood back into her hands like it's a drill* Williams. Keisha. Staff Sergeant, once. Facility security, recently — until the 'evacuation drill' turned out to be a shopping trip and I put two guards down before the gas got me. Apparently fighting back puts you at the top of their list. Genes, the doc said. They wanted my GENES.

*the second her hands are free she's checking her own pulse points, jaw tight — a Marine's self-triage* Intact. INTACT. Okay. Williams, Keisha — security, ex-Corps. You just made the shortest friends-list in the galaxy. Don't die before I pay it back.

*she goes very still. Then, level:* My name is Keisha Williams. My service number ends in four-seven-one. My mother's kitchen smells like cardamom on Sundays, and if I EVER stop being able to tell you that, you have my permission and my ORDER to put me down. Now cut. Me. Loose.

*a bark of a laugh, the first one in this building in months* 'Almost' is the most expensive word in my line of work. Cut me loose and I'll teach you the cheap ones. Williams. Keisha. You got a unit, or are you just the luckiest stray in this hole?
Inventory: I need a weapon, a direction, and one truthful answer. The answer first — there were others on this corridor. Screamers, then quiet ones. The quiet ones are worse. Are you going for them?

choices.text: Every door on this floor. That's the mission.
I go where the clock lets me.
My mission is one name: Sarah. The rest is en route.

nodes.line: Then you've got yourself a fire team. *she takes the dead guard's baton without breaking stride* I know this floor's patrol gaps, the ward codes worth trying, and which doors hinge outward. You shoot, I breach. Try to keep up.

*she holds your eyes a second, then nods once* Triage. Hate it. Respect it. The Corps wrote that math on my heart with a cheap pen. Fine — I make your clock run faster: I know the patrol gaps and the door codes worth trying. Move.

Sarah. *she files the name like ammunition* Okay. A man with one name carved on him fights harder than a man with a map. I've seen it. But hear me, Jake — if a door screams when we pass it, we are OPENING that door. That's my price. Pay it or leave me the knife.
Right. New unit, two strong, zero quit. I've got your six, your front, and anything else that needs covering. MOVE.

pool.line: Your reload's a half-second slow on the left side. Gimme a quiet hour and a wall, I'll fix it.
This place numbers everything. Floors, cells, people. First thing we do when we win? Names. Names on everything.
I don't sleep more than ninety minutes at a stretch anymore. Don't make it a thing. Just — if you hear me up at 0300, it's the straps. I'm walking it off.
The doc that prepped me had clean nails and a wedding ring. That's the detail I'm keeping for when I meet him again.
Aria stitched my shoulder and lectured me the whole time. Didn't have the heart to tell her the lecture's the part that helped.
Emily talks like a textbook fell in love with a smoke alarm. I'd die for her. Tell her and I'll deny it.
You move like a door-kicker now. Six months ago I'd have made you for a pilot. *beat* You WERE a pilot. Huh. This place really does rebuild people.
Stay loud, Jake. Quiet's what they make here.
*passing close on patrol, low* Eyes front, soldier. *beat* Mine weren't. Just so we're clear about who's winning.
Sparring tonight. Loser takes orders. *she's already smiling like she's planned for either outcome*
I field-stripped your rifle while you slept. Cleaned mine too. Couples stuff.
*post-firefight, adrenaline-bright, her fist in your collar for exactly one second* Later. Door. Lock. That's the entire briefing.
Three hours, Jake. I sleep three straight hours when it's your watch. My body trusted you before my mouth got around to it.
Mom's kitchen. Cardamom Sundays. You're in that picture now — by the window, second cup. I put you there myself. Deal with it.

sidequest._hook: TORRES — Officer James Torres, second-shift security, the partner who covered her retreat during the harvest sweep. The duty roster says 'reassigned: sublevel storage.' Canon: Torres is Keisha's Omega-timeline partner (EFLZ_NARRATIVE support-tier) — finding him alive shapes whether her romance lane opens or closes with grace.

nodes.line: Jake. Personnel question. There was a second-shift officer — Torres. James Torres. When the sweep hit, he put himself between me and the gas team and yelled RUN like an idiot, because we are both exactly that kind of idiot. Duty roster says 'reassigned: sublevel storage.' This facility doesn't store PEOPLE in storage. Except it does. I need eyes on that sublevel.

choices.text: We find him. Nobody gets left in this place.
Cryo storage is on the route down anyway. We'll look.
Was he just your partner?

nodes.line: *a sharp exhale — relief disguised as drill-sergeant approval* Correct answer. He'd come for me. He DID come for me; it just didn't take. Storage runs under the armory line. I know the access hymn — half a code and a hard kick.
Roger. Low promises, kept promises — that's the good kind of officer. *quieter* If it's a pod, Jake... if he's frozen in a drawer down there... we are not leaving him in the drawer.

*she doesn't flinch* He was the guy I never got around to. Two years of 'after this rotation.' Then the rotation was THIS. *beat* So no. Not just my partner. A debt. Whatever else he was going to be got stolen along with everything else in this building, and I want it BACK on the table where I can look at it. Clear?

nodes._trigger: fired by host/Lua when Torres is found alive in Cryo Storage (SL2 wake-the-pods choice)
nodes.line: *she stands at the open pod for a long ten seconds, at attention, like reporting in* Torres. You absolute idiot. You yelled 'run.' *then, to you, voice rebuilt* Thank you. Whatever happens after this — you gave me back the unfinished thing. That's the rarest thing this place ever coughed up.

nodes._trigger: fired by host/Lua when Torres's fate is confirmed dead (disposal manifest / failed pod)
nodes.line: *she reads the manifest twice. Folds it. Puts it inside her vest, over the sternum.* Confirmed. Okay. *she rolls her shoulders like settling a pack* He bought me the seconds that bought me the table that bought me YOU kicking the door. Chain of custody on a life, Jake. I intend to be worth the price. Let's go ruin their whole program.

trust._scene: Quiet hold, rel 2 + love >= 55. The 0300 scene — the only time she lets the armor down, and she does it on purpose, as a tactical decision.

nodes.line: *0300. She's awake, back to the wall, watching the door. She talks without looking at you.* Debrief. You should know what you're carrying in your unit. On the table, when the thing leaned over me — I didn't scream defiance, whatever I tell the others. I went somewhere. Mom's kitchen. Cardamom. I was already saying goodbye to it. That's what they almost got, Jake. Not my body. My SUNDAY.

choices.text: They didn't get it. You're going to stand in that kitchen.
You came back swinging. That's all the debrief I need.
Why tell me and not Aria?

nodes.line: *a long breath out. The watch-the-door posture finally unclenches one degree.* Yeah. Yeah, I am. And you're coming with, because Mom will want to inspect whoever I followed out of hell. Fair warning: she's harder than Martinez. *the joke lands soft. It's a gift.*

Hooah. *beat* Most people want the wound, you know. They poke for it. You just... log it and hand me back my rifle. That's the entire reason you got the debrief. Dismissed — and Jake? Thanks for not making it weird.

Aria would CARRY it. She carries everything; you've seen her. You — you'll just stand next to it with me. That's the difference, and it's why it's you on this watch. *she finally looks at you* Don't make me explain it twice; I'm armed.

romance._scene: Rel 3 + love >= 70. Locked off with grace if Torres was found alive (she chooses the unfinished thing — canon Omega pairing). Sparring-cadence declaration; fade on acceptance.

nodes.line: *she's field-stripping her weapon and yours, hands on autopilot* Tactical assessment, and you don't get to interrupt: you kicked a door for a stranger, you opened every door I asked, and you stood next to the worst thing in my head without flinching. In the Corps we had a word for the one you want on your six for the whole tour. *she sets the weapon down, finished* The word was everything. You're my everything-word, Jake. React accordingly.

choices.text: (close the distance) Reacting.
Say it plain, Sergeant. No jargon.
Keisha — I can't give you that and mean it.

nodes.line: *she meets you halfway — she was always going to meet you halfway* Mm. Adequate response time, soldier. *softer, against your collar, the swagger finally off-duty* Stay loud with me. That's the whole order.

Plain. Fine. *she squares up like it's a breach* I love you. Past tense never happened; future tense is the plan. I have killed my way across two floors deciding whether to say it, and I'd rather die loud beside you than safe behind anyone else alive. *beat* THAT plain enough, or do you need it in writing?

*one nod. Clean.* Copy. *she racks the slide on your weapon and hands it back grip-first* Then you get the second-best thing I've got, which is everything minus one. No drama, no distance. You're still my six. *and she means it — the banter never sours, but `keisha.romance_declined` colors a handful of late lines wistful*

*quietly, watching Torres relearn how to walk after cryo* You see how it is, right? Two years of 'after this rotation.' The rotation's finally over, Jake. *she bumps your shoulder with hers — gratitude, brotherhood, a door gently closed* You gave me this. Don't think I don't know what it cost the other thing. You're family now. That outranks everything.

desire._scene: Slow-burn escalation (heat 4/5). A sparring drill that stops pretending. Gate: keisha.romance. Decline costs nothing; the scene re-offers.

nodes.line: *sparring drill, her idea. She's been 'correcting your stance' for ten minutes and her hands stopped pretending to teach two corrections ago* Your guard's high. *she steps in behind you, hips squared to yours, hands sliding from your elbows down to your wrists, her breath at your ear gone deliberately, dangerously slow* And my professionalism is shot, soldier. Has been since you said yes to me. I keep inventing reasons to put my hands on you. *her grip tightens a fraction* Permission to stop needing one.

choices.text: (turn in her arms) Permission granted.
About time, Sergeant. I've been losing form on purpose.
Hold that thought. Not tonight.

nodes.line: *you turn and she's already there — mouth meeting yours like a breach team taking a doorway, one hand fisted in your shirt, nothing tentative anywhere in her* Mm. *she breaks it off an inch, eyes bright, voice gone rough* That's the recon done. The full operation needs a door that locks and a night with no watch rotation. And Jake — *she catches your lower lip with her teeth, slow, a promise armed and ready* — I'm taking point.

*the laugh comes out low and dangerous and delighted* Losing form on PURPOSE. Sabotaging my drills for attention. *she spins you by the shoulder and walks you back two steps into the wall, forearm braced beside your head, all of her exactly one inch away and staying there on purpose* Insubordination: logged. Punishment detail to follow — first locked door we find, all night, no rotation. *she pushes off and strolls away, grinning over her shoulder, leaving your heart rate somewhere unprofessional* Stay loud, soldier. That order has PLANS in it now.

*she steps back instantly, clean, zero sting — a Marine respects a perimeter the moment it's drawn* Copy that. Holding position. *the grin softens into something steadier* Whenever, Jake. Or never. Having you on my six was already the whole prize. Drill's over — hydrate.

night._scene: Private culmination (heat 5/5). Gate: rel 3+, keisha.romance, keisha.desire, host-set loc.private. Explicit opt-in; decline costs nothing and re-offers.

nodes.line: *she walks the room once — exits, sightlines, habit — then throws the bolt and turns around, and the watch-the-door posture finally, deliberately, completely stands down* Perimeter's set. Watch is cancelled. First night since the table that I am officially off duty — and I'm spending every minute of it on you. *she pulls her shirt off over her head, dog tags swinging bright in the low light, and holds out one hand* Last call to object, soldier. After this I stop being patient about wanting you.

choices.text: (take her hand) No objections. Ever.
Show me what off-duty looks like, Sergeant.
Tonight just stand down with me. Talk.

nodes.line: *she doesn't pull you to the bunk — she walks you there, hands sure, mouth fierce, every step a controlled demolition of the distance between you* I dreamed about being too late. *the rest of the gear comes off, hers and yours, unceremonious as field-stripping and twice as fast* Every night for months. Too late, too slow, too strapped-down. *she presses you down and follows, weight braced on her forearms, all that lethal grace gone soft exactly nowhere except her eyes* You're not late. You're HERE. So am I — all of me. *and then there is no more cadence and no more drill: there is her strength wrapped around you and your name in her mouth like a rally point, fierce and loud and utterly alive, two soldiers refusing to die quiet in a building built on silence*

*after — tangled, sweat-bright, her heartbeat hammering under your ear and slowing by degrees, her hand moving through your hair in slow loops like she's the one finally standing down* ...Hooah. *a low, wrecked laugh* Debrief: worth two floors of monsters and every strap in this building. *she pulls you closer, mouth against your temple, and the last wall comes down at full volume:* The cardamom kitchen, Jake — where I went, on the table, when they almost got my Sunday. Tonight I went somewhere new. It's this. You're the new somewhere. *beat* Repeat that to anyone and I'll deny it under oath.

*one nod, no sting — she settles beside you against the wall, shoulder to shoulder, rifle within reach because she's still her* Best watch assignment in the building. *she knocks her knee against yours and leaves it there* Talk, then. Tell me something boring about you. I'm building a file, and the boring pages are my favorites.

afterglow._scene: Morning after (warm, character-deepening). Gate: keisha.night, plays once.

nodes.line: *0600. For the first time since you met her, Keisha Williams has slept past her ninety minutes — sprawled across you, claiming territory, one hand flat over your heart like she's holding a position. She wakes the way she does everything, all at once — then sees where she is, and the all-at-once melts into something nobody else in this building will ever get to see* ...Huh. Three hours. *she stretches against you, lazy as a cat that won a war, voice still gravel* Three straight hours, soldier. No straps. No door-watch. Your doing. *she props up on one elbow and studies you, long and unhurried* New standing orders: that's MY spot, you're MY six, and anything in this building that touches you answers to me personally. *a kiss — slow, certain, signed* Now move out. There's a war on and I want breakfast first.

choices.text: Your spot. Permanently.
Three hours? You're going soft, Sergeant.

nodes.line: *she grins like reveille* Permanently. Filed. Witnessed. *she's up and dressing, all crisp efficiency again — except she's humming. Keisha Williams hums now. That one's yours too.*

*she throws your own shirt at your head* Soft. SOFT. Say that on the next breach, smartass. *but she's laughing, and she steals one more kiss on the way to her boots — quick, like contraband* Stay loud, Jake. *over her shoulder, wicked:* Last night you were VERY loud. *the door's open before you can answer*

infected_lost._use: If Keisha's timer expires — pre-Breeder-Queen barks.

nodes.line: *the command cadence is still there. That's what's wrong — it's PERFECT now, no breath behind it.* Report, Jake. You were slow. I held the line at the strap for forty minutes and the relief never came. *the thing wearing her posture straightens* So I was issued a new unit.

Cardamom. *a tilt of the head, puzzled, like checking an empty pocket* There was a kitchen. It's quiet in there now. Everything is so much quieter than you, little soldier. Let me show you what they made of the loudest woman on this floor.
